items.title: The root spaces of the extended graph form the irreducible integrable highest weight module of highest weight w
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the identification of the direct sum of the root spaces of the extended graph with an irreducible integrable highest weight representation and the resulting root-multiplicity formula (author Lemma at source lines 1184-1196, label lem:root). The proof (source lines 1198-1217) does two things: it reads off the commutation relations with the raising operators from the definition of the extended graph, and then shows that the prescribed root space is spanned by iterated brackets of the lowering operators with f_infinity, using a displayed bracket identity that moves f_infinity across the bracket up to a sign (proof lines 1203-1211). That spanning statement is what makes V a highest weight module with highest weight vector f_infinity; integrability and the translation of root multiplicities into weight multiplicities are attributed to two specific sections of Kac's book (proof lines 1213-1215). The step with content is the bracket identity and the spanning conclusion, not the citation. H2.
